public_comment.topic: Urged that any candidate screening for board/committee appointments stay in one open, transparent meeting rather than a separate subcommittee process.

minutes.headline: Town warns the FY27 budget season will be rough amid finance-office vacancies and a 30% Nashoba fee hike
minutes.summary: The Select Board made routine appointments (historical commission delegate, register of voters, conservation agent at step five, a part-time librarian) and opened the annual town meeting warrant. Most of the meeting was the town manager and board warning that finance-department staffing vacancies are straining every department heading into a difficult FY27 budget season, alongside news of a 30% Nashoba Associated Boards of Health assessment increase and a water-billing correction affecting 11 customers.

votes.motion: Appoint Jennifer Sanderson to the APDC as the historical commission representative, term to expire June 2027.
Appoint Shirley McBride to the register of voters, term to expire March 31, 2028.
Ratify the town manager's appointment of Herin/Hurland Jamie as conservation agent and approve a step five salary.
Approve the two ABCC annual certification forms.
Open the annual town meeting warrant on January 6, 2026 and close it on March 16, 2026.
Approve the listed sets of minutes (multiple dates read aloud, including one from December 16).

budget_items.what_was_said: The town manager sought approval of a step five salary for the new conservation agent based on her education and experience.

budget_items.topic: Nashoba Associated Boards of Health assessment
budget_items.what_was_said: The town manager reported Nashoba voted to raise its assessment, citing a structural funding shortfall from declining land-use revenue and expiring COVID-era grant funding.
The increase over what the town had already anticipated, and the resulting total assessment, were stated.

Eleven customers who missed regular quarterly water bills due to a staffing-transition administrative breakdown will receive catch-up bills covering roughly a year of usage; a rate adjustment is expected on a near-term agenda.
The board reviewed an accounts payable warrant for signature.
A board member reported the school committee's budget workshop found paraprofessionals that had not been accounted for in the FY26 budget, with details to follow in a superintendent's letter.

budget_items.topic: School budget vote timing vs. town manager's number
budget_items.what_was_said: The school administration recommended the school committee vote on its own budget before receiving the town manager's budget number, to present a clear ask to the town manager and tri-board.
The town manager described the coming budget season as anticipated to be financially challenging, compounded by finance-department staffing vacancies.

budget_items.topic: Warrant article for senior center mailer
budget_items.what_was_said: A board member asked to place a warrant article for a town mailer on an upcoming agenda, to work it out with the board before bringing it to the council on aging, ahead of the busiest budget-meeting period.

decisions.decision: The board will hold a workshop on the special event policy at next week's meeting.
The board agreed not to move forward with a subcommittee-based screening step for the appointment policy, in response to public and member feedback.
A rate adjustment related to water billing is expected to be placed on next Tuesday's agenda.
The chair will stop routinely including the select board bylaw item on the agenda unless a member has something specific to raise for the bylaw review committee.
Add a warrant article for a town mailer (for the council on aging) to an upcoming agenda before budget meetings intensify.

what_happened.line: The town manager and board warned the FY27 budget season will be difficult, worsened by vacancies in the finance department.
Nashoba Associated Boards of Health voted to raise its assessment on the town, citing a structural funding shortfall.
Eleven water customers missed regular quarterly bills after a staffing-transition breakdown and will get catch-up bills; a rate adjustment is expected next week.
A school committee budget workshop found paraprofessionals left out of the FY26 school budget; a superintendent's letter is expected to explain the correction.
The board voted to open the annual town meeting warrant, to close March 16, 2026.

why_it_matters: A strained finance office heading into budget season can slow the numbers residents will eventually vote on at town meeting.
A higher regional health assessment and an FY26 school budget correction both press on the same town budget that funds services and schools.
The eleven affected water customers will see a larger-than-usual bill covering roughly a year of missed usage, and other customers may see a rate change follow.
